newsitem.title: POLAND: British ship snags wartime shell in Polish port.
newsitem.headline: British ship snags wartime shell in Polish port.

text.p: A British ship has snagged a World War Two artillery shell in its anchor chain in the Polish port of Swinoujscie and a storm has stopped navy sappers from removing it.

"A mud-encased shell of about 20 cm (eight inches) in diameter was hauled up by the British ship Jevington as it was about to leave port," port duty officer Ryszard Stanczyk told PAP news agency on Sunday.
"The ship is waiting to have the shell removed but stormy seas and wind are making this difficult," he added. He said the winds were blowing at force six -- about 25 miles (40 km) per hour.

Commodore Piotr Andrzejewski told PAP the navy could not guarantee the safety of other ships in the port and suggested the Jevington should moor at the north quay where sappers would attempt to remove the dangling shell.
